explanation: Beijing lies at about 40° N, 116° E, so its opposite point is about 40° S, 64° W, in Argentina. Tunnel from most of the United States and you would surface in the Indian Ocean.

claims.text: The antipode of Beijing, at about 40° S, 64° W, lies in Argentina.
The antipode of Beijing does not lie in Chile, Brazil or the United States.
Beijing lies at about 40° N, 116° E.
The antipodes of most of the contiguous United States lie in the Indian Ocean.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: content:check reports no errors or warnings for this item. Claims: every checkable statement is listed; c1 and c3 carry coordinates and c4 says 'most', so all are high; c2 is standard. Datasets: geonames-cities: Beijing CN admin1 22 lat 39.9075, lng 116.39723 (c3). The antipode is lat -39.9075, lng -63.60277; a point-in-polygon test against natural-earth ne_110m_admin_0_countries puts it inside Argentina (c1, c2). For c4 I took a 0.5° grid of 3,350 points inside the contiguous United States polygon: none of their antipodes falls on land at the 110m scale, and all lie between 25° and 49° S and 55° and 113° E, in the Indian Ocean. Rival test: the United States is the trap from the 'dig a hole to China' saying run in reverse; Chile is the near miss on the same latitude, but at 64° W the point is well east of the Andes; Brazil does not reach 40° S. A good reasoner can get there: flip the hemisphere and add 180° of longitude. Against the key: none. Volatility: evergreen, settled geography with no review date; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: uses only coordinates and a world map. Style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, straight quotes, explanation of 35 words. Myths: every claim screened against content/reference/myths.json; no match. Mystery and encore: nothing of either kind to check in a practice item. Doubts: none.

claimResults.note: Antipode computed as latitude times -1 and longitude minus 180, from geonames-cities Beijing. About 40° S, 64° W.
So it is in none of Chile, Brazil or the United States.

evidence.locator: ADMIN=United States of America, mainland polygon; every country polygon
evidence.excerpt: 3350 grid points at 0.5° spacing inside the mainland polygon; antipodes on land: 0; antipode range 55.5 to 112.5° E, 25.5 to 49° S

claimResults.note: Every sampled antipode falls in open ocean between Africa and Australia, north of 60° S, so in the Indian Ocean. The 110m file omits a few tiny islands there (Amsterdam, Saint-Paul, Kerguelen), which leaves 'most' intact.

evidence.locator: point-in-polygon of the antipode of Beijing (GeoNames 39.9075 N, 116.39723 E)

claimResults.note: About 110 km inland from the 110m coastline vertex, so the coarse scale does not matter.

evidence.excerpt: Only Argentina contains the antipode, so not Chile, Brazil or the United States

evidence.excerpt: 3350 grid points; 0 antipodes on land; antipode longitudes 55.5 to 112.5 E, latitudes -49.0 to -25.5: the southern Indian Ocean

claimResults.note: The 110m file omits small islands such as Kerguelen, which a thin northern sliver of the US maps to, so 'most' is the right word.

editor.reason: Both checks pass with every claim confirmed; high-risk c1, c3 and c4 carry natural-earth and geonames-cities evidence in both checks (§9.9 rule 3). Lint clean, no myth hits. Dedupe pairs it with p.hist.0225 (same answer): that item asks about Eva Perón, a different fact.

stem: If you tunnelled straight through Earth's centre from Beijing, in which country would you come out?
